SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a best-in-class coatings franchise with durable structural advantages (~5,000 company-operated stores, high contractor switching costs, 49% gross margins, 47-year dividend streak). Q1 2026 results were solid: revenue +6.8% YoY, adjusted EPS beat consensus by 4.9%, and management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of $11.50–$11.90 adjusted EPS. However, the stock is not yet compelling enough for a higher score. Trailing PE of 29.1x sits at the bottom of its 365-day range (28.5–37.1x), but the 3.4% earnings yield remains below the 4.45% 10-year Treasury, and forward adjusted PE of ~26x on guidance is fair but not cheap for a mid-single-digit grower facing a +30% oil cost headwind and 2.1x+ leverage. The housing-linked end markets remain challenged with management expecting little recovery in 2026. The valuation compression is driven by legitimate macro repricing (rates, oil) rather than creating deep value. A mild positive score reflects the high-quality franchise, positive earnings trajectory, and valuation near the low end of its range, but the macro headwinds (rates, oil input costs) and lack of a near-term fundamental catalyst cap upside.
key_factors: Q1 2026 revenue $5.67B, +6.8% YoY; adjusted EPS $2.35 beat consensus $2.24 by 4.9%
Gross margin stable at 49% across multiple quarters, indicating durable pricing power
PE diluted 29.1x at bottom decile of 365-day range (28.5–37.1x); P/B 17.1x near trough (16.7–22.1x)
Forward adjusted PE ~26x on FY2026 guidance of $11.50–$11.90, more reasonable than trailing 29.1x
Earnings yield 3.4% below 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%, requiring growth to justify premium
WTI crude surged +30.3% to $92.65/bbl, a meaningful headwind for petroleum-based feedstock costs
Total debt elevated at $11.7B (per earnings call) with net debt/EBITDA of 2.5x; rising rates increase service costs
Management expects little to no recovery in most end markets in 2026; housing cycle remains challenged
~5,000 company-operated stores in North America create structural competitive moat difficult to replicate
Returned $772.7M to shareholders in Q1 ($575.6M buybacks, $197.1M dividends); 47-year dividend increase streak
AkzoNobel-Axalta merger would create ~$17B competitor, narrowing gap but still meaningfully smaller than SHW
Price down -15.4% over past quarter to $305.14, in bottom quartile of 365-day range ($294.32–$379.65)
